text:
anya: Quick design review — thinking about switching the roles selector in the invite flow to horizontal "pills" with collapsible details per role. Goal: fewer clicks, faster scan, and make permission summaries more visible. Sketch: https://figma.redwood/example :link:

matt: Interesting. Pills feel lightweight. Concern: long role names will wrap and break the layout on small widths. Could we truncate + show full name on hover? :thinking_face:

rui: Agree with truncation + tooltip. Also keyboard accessibility: each pill should be a focusable button with `aria-pressed` state. For collapsible details use `aria-expanded` on the pill and `aria-controls` to point to the detail panel. Example: "<button aria-pressed=\"false\" aria-expanded=\"false\">Viewer</button>"

anya: Nice, Rui — like the idea. UX question: when a pill expands, do we push the rest of the chips down (accordion behavior) or open an overlay panel? I worry about page jump.

matt: Overlay seems less disruptive but hides context (you lose glanceability of other roles). Push-down accordion is more discoverable. If we do push-down, we must ensure the focus stays on the expanded content and that screen readers get a live region announcement.

sarah: For copy, if we keep accordion: header copy should be concise: e.g., "Viewer — can read org resources" and detail copy: "Can view projects, logs, and audit entries. Does not allow invites." If overlay/modal: primary CTA inside should be "Select role" and secondary "Cancel". For SSO toggle confirmation language propose: "Enable SSO for this org? Users without SSO will be blocked from signing in. This cannot be undone without admin support."

ken: From product telemetry POV, if we change to pills we should track: `role_pill_expand`, `role_assigned_via_pills`, and `role_tooltip_view`. Also watch for significant delta in invite completion time.

anya: Accessibility nit — ensure focus ring is visible on high-contrast themes. Also for truncated names, `aria-label` should include full role name + short permission summary.

rui: One more accessibility thing: audit log navigation. When somebody clicks a role from the invite flow and then navigates to audit logs, we should preserve filters (role=selected) and provide a visible breadcrumb: "Invites > Viewer (filtered)". Keyboard users should be able to clear the filter with a single `Esc` when the filter dropdown is focused.

matt: Implementation question: how do we handle SSO-enabled orgs? If SSO is ON, should some roles be hidden or annotated? My vote: annotate with a small lock icon and tooltip: "SSO enforced — assignment will require SSO-linked accounts". Also confirm modal for toggling SSO should require typing org name if changing enforcement to OFF.

anya: Good call. For the confirm modal copy we propose this block (rough):
```
Title: Confirm SSO enforcement change
Body: Turning SSO enforcement off may allow users to sign in without your identity provider. To proceed, type your org name: <org-name>
Primary CTA: Confirm change
Secondary CTA: Cancel
```

sarah: Minor copy tweak: replace "Turning SSO enforcement off" with "Disabling SSO enforcement" — more direct. And change Primary CTA to "Confirm disable" to be explicit.

design-bot: design-assets: updated — /components/roles/pills v1.2 uploaded to Figma. :white_check_mark:

anya: Next steps:
- Rui to draft aria attributes & keyboard flow doc (due EOD Thu)
- Matt to mock responsive truncation + tooltip behavior (Figma frame)
- Sarah to finalize CTAs and confirmation copy
- Ken to add telemetry events to the backlog

matt: ack :thumbsup:

rui: will do, adding notes about screen-reader announcements :eyes:

sarah: I'll run copy through legal for the SSO modal wording, will update thread when done.

ken: will add tracking spikes for invite flow sandbox.

anya: Thanks all — we'll reconvene after the mocks. :sparkles:
